title: On-demand and slots: two pricing models and how to choose

videos.script: Every BigQuery query is paid for in one of two ways. {{two}} On demand, you pay for the bytes it reads. Eleven dollars and a quarter a tebibyte, in São Paulo. {{ondemand}} A query that reads too little still pays for ten megabytes. And LIMIT saves nothing. {{rules}} On slots, you pay for the compute instead, by the slot-hour, in one of three editions. {{editions}} Slots can grow and shrink with the work. Each step is fifty slots, billed for at least a minute. {{autoscale}} So a dashboard of tiny queries can cost two hundred and fifty times the work it did. {{tiny}} Where the two models meet is a single ratio: slot-hours for every tebibyte read. {{ratio}} You will compute it with a short program, and choose a model for two of Quitanda's workloads. {{choose}} Then the guardrails, set before the query that costs a fortune arrives. {{guard}}
